newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch BNG mulls taking stake in Belgium's CCB.
newsitem.headline: Dutch BNG mulls taking stake in Belgium's CCB.

text.p: Dutch local authorities bank, Bank Nederlandse Gemeenten (BNG), said on Wednesday it was considering taking a stake of about three percent in its Belgian publicly-owned counterpart, Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet (CCB).
BNG already owns three percent of French bank Credit Local de France (CLF), which is forming an alliance with CCB involving cross-shareholdings.

"The only possibility that we might look at, next to the participation we have in Credit Local, is that we might also take a participation (shareholding) in CCB," BNG's senior vice-president Treasury, Bert de Kock, said in an interview.
He said that in doing so, BNG would maintain its interest in the CLF/CCB group.
"But no decision has been made yet (on) whether we are going to take a participation at all. It's under consideration," de Kock said.
BNG, which finances Dutch public authorities, lifted its stake in CLF, the leading provider of finance to French local authorities, to three percent from one percent last year.
They have a co-operation agreement to jointly finance European local authorities.
